summary.text: 非 is an old graph whose early form has been read either as wings facing apart or as two people back-to-back. Oracle-bone examples already use it as a negative; the evidence does not show that this use developed from either picture.

formation.text: Pictographic interpretations are recorded, but the referent is disputed: the received Shuowen account sees opposed wings, while Wang Qingju proposes two people back-to-back. Neither reading is settled by the supplied evidence, and no internal phonetic component is established. The selected oracle-script-style image is a modern redraw, not an ancient artifact photograph.

components.text: The whole early graph is interpreted either as two wings facing away from one another or as two people back-to-back. The graph evidence supplied here does not decide between these readings; treat the entire form as the picture rather than splitting it into modern-looking parts.

sound_limitation.text: No phonetic component in 非’s own graphic formation is established in the inspected analyses; character readings do not establish a component-level sound role.

history.text: The received Shuowen explanation describes 非 as opposition and interprets its form as the lower wings of 飛 facing away. This is a historical explanation, not proof of the graph’s original referent or a dated route from that referent to negation. A competing proposal reads early forms as people back-to-back and relates 非 to 北; the dossier does not resolve these accounts.

The curated Shang oracle-script-style illustration is a modern vector redraw associated with an identified Xiaoxuetang record, not an artifact photograph. The dossier reports oracle-bone, bronze, bamboo/slip, and seal forms, but that inventory does not establish a complete sequence of graphic changes.

uncertainties.text: The original referent and graphic origin remain unresolved. Early forms have competing wing and human readings; the proposed relation to 北 is not independently verified, and the supplied evidence does not settle a relation to 飛.

Oracle-bone examples already include negative uses, but the evidence does not establish whether negation developed from an earlier pictorial or opposition sense. The proposed 不 + 惟 fusion concerns the spoken word, remains disputed, and does not establish that the graph is composed of those characters.
No phonetic component in 非’s own formation is established in the inspected analyses, so the character’s readings do not support a component-level sound comparison.

senses.text: Reported oracle-bone examples use 非 as a negative. The dossier identifies oracle-bone script as the earliest script class in its evidence, but does not establish an absolute date for the examples.

senses.period: Han-era dictionary explanation; earlier use unresolved
senses.text: The received Shuowen explanation glosses 非 as opposition and connects that sense with wings facing away. This records an interpretation, not an independently established early lexical stage.

senses.gloss: fault or wrongness; judging something wrong
senses.period: bronze inscriptions reported; absolute date unresolved
senses.text: Reported bronze examples use 非 for faults and for judging something wrong. Their relation in time or meaning to the early negative use is not established here.
Later dictionary records include uses meaning reproach or criticize; their listing does not establish a complete chronology or a semantic path from the negative sense.
A later dictionary records an avoid sense. The supplied evidence does not establish its relation to the other senses.
Modern references give negative meanings including ‘not’ and ‘non-’.

limitations.text: The early negative attestations do not establish whether this sense developed from a pictorial meaning or from opposition; no dated semantic transition is supplied.
Reported uses for wrongness, reproach, and avoidance do not establish a complete chronology or the links among those senses and negation.
The proposed 不 + 惟 fusion is a disputed account of the spoken word 非. It is not evidence that the graph was formed from 不 and 惟, and it does not identify the name of a depicted object.

overview.text: 非 is an old graph used as a negative from the oracle-bone period. Its early picture is disputed: it may show opposed wings or two people back-to-back; neither reading explains a proven path to ‘not’.

components.text: Treat the whole graph as one disputed picture: opposed wings in one account, or two people back-to-back in another. The evidence does not settle which.
